notes.title: v 1.36 Attacking enemies and starting resources
notes.content:
Hi all!

I've got some new feedback, I did some brainstorming, and here's how I addressed it.

Some of you complained that they do struggle with enemies attacking the towers. Now this is a quite fundamental feature of EiR, designed to be different by classic Tower Defense in such a way that you can't just build tower and wait, but you need to be active in maintaining them and adapting your techniques.

I though, though, that if some of you would like it different, why not? Now in Game Settings there's an option (only available when not in battle obviously) to deactivate the enemies AI attack capability. Special abilities will still work though, including the Brute ability to damage towers, but you shan't fear anymore the standard units to attack and damage your towers. This will make maps a lot easier, and it will reduce the score to 65% of the max score, so that leaderboards still stay consistent, but we hope you like the option!

I also increased the bonus given in starting battle gold by the province from which you attack (and fixed a bug that prevented the updated value to be visualized at battle start). You now receive +1% for each 10 units of gold production of the attacking province. (before it was +1% each 50 units). Keep in mind that if the province is using the resources to build, it will not provide any bonus in that case.

[b]v1.36[/b]
[list]
[*] Added option in Game Settings that prevents enemies from attacking towers (Specialy abilities still work though, including the ones that cause damage like the one from the Brute)
[*] Increased the bonus to starting Gold in battle given by the gold production of the attacking province. You now receive +1% every 10 units of gold produced. (before ti was every 50 units).
[*] Fixed a bug that didn't show increased starting gold at battle start
[/list]

Cheers!
Dr.H

notes.title: A guide to Scout Towers
notes.content:
Hi, 

A few of you, in the last few weeks, seemed to find the Scout Towers a "useless waste of resource". Well then, I am here to clarify why I have to disagree with it, and why I think the little straw-capped fellas are more than useful, in theory and practice! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/945d9498323f889394029d0c46aab7bb19b00654.jpg[/img]

After some of the recent feedback, I did further lower the Scout Towers building and repair costs too, but let me start with a list of the reasons why I think they are useful.

[list]
[*] Without Scout Towers you will have no information about enemy waves until they appeared in map (aka too late to build anything)
[*] Scout Towers are the only mean to detect the Sappers special paths (tunnels, forest paths or blown up rocks)
[*] Flying Enemies don't follow any standard path and have the ability to damage the headquarters also upon death. Scout Towers are the only mean to detect them and destroy them far enough from the Headquarters.
[*] Skirmishers are invisible to the attack towers unless in the area of a Scout Tower, Rangers or Temple with the Eye of Kaer ability activated. In order to kill them in time, detecting the Skirmishers far enough from the Headquarters is often vital.
[*] Scout Towers are very cheap (after the last update even cheaper)
[*] A Scout Tower can be used as a cheap decoy to draw enemies damage abilities away from the attack towers. Build a Scout Tower in front (and far enough) from a Repeating Crossbow, to make sure Brutes and Steam Carriages won't take your best tower down and leave undamaged.
[*] Upgrading a Scout Tower to Outpost Tower is cheap (it's also been lowered with the last update) and will make the Tower resistant to fire (and therefore a lot more robust against Sappers' and Gliders' fire bombs)
[*] Outpost Towers have no attack abilities, but can be endowed with Caltrops (that cause continuous damage to enemies nearby) and Nets (that slow down passing enemies).
[/list]

As you can see, the Scout Tower has been designed to be a quite flexible asset. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/e0fdf1884da342f7af7633481607389ee5094f17.jpg[/img]

While in the first maps you can live with not knowing where the enemies are coming from (as long as you cluster all of your towers next to the Headquarters), in the later maps, being able to predict the exact paths of the next wave will allow you spread out your towers for a far more efficient killing ground. 

Once the Steam Carriages are in game, using Scout Towers as a decoy to protect your larger towers, becomes really paramount, as their front-mounted cannons can easily take out one tower with one shot otherwise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/f879c1d4c3bc941ef9ba6c0ae9d6cfe62af66d10.jpg[/img]

I hope this clarified a few things, if you got question, ask away, I hope I also got answers for you!
Cheers,
Dr.H

notes.title: Research in Arcade Mode
notes.content:
During the Early Access months (btw, only 20 days left), we got a few "complains" that Arcade mode, while for many the less interesting one due to the lack of the management parts, felt like it was just an afterthought and not a really independent play mode.

The main reason being the lack of a sense of progression and of a tech tree system like in the campaign and sandbox. Well well, don't say we don't listen! Here comes the full Tech Tree and Research System for the Arcade mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/a005eacb0a32931cf0c44a0768925e5517a9a5ce.jpg[/img]

It's similar, but also has quite a few differences, if compared to the campaign and sandbox one. First of all, it's not turn based. It means that buying a research is instantaneous as long as you have Research points to spend. Points are earned through victories, the same victories unlocking the next maps too.

The first time you achieve stars  in each of the Difficulties you achieve an equivalent number of research points (thankfully, each difficulty also provide the missing stars on the lower difficulties, so if you get 3 stars in Hardcore mode, you don't have to replay in easy and intermediate to unlock the other stars, and you get them right away). If you get 3 Stars in Hardcore mode, you earn a bonus Research point for the golden medal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/e59abc2e8ac70bc6b7c879242b0c849ed5cb3d20.jpg[/img]

Cooldown abilities and Temples, that in the campaign are not handled through research, are also unlockable the same way. We did some testing already, but we would really really like to get your feedback about the new system.

Ah, we introduced a reset method for Arcade mode, in case you already had stars and wanna start scoring some research points: [i][b][u]hold left shift + hold right shift + tap Y[/u][/b][/i] on your keyboard. This will reset your full arcade progress and system, and you can now start earning research points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/240b5c11f315c917094fee7ceb8d756603e05ba8.jpg[/img]

Ah, this you will like. We also added a new shooting mode, Flying Enemies First, it should save you a lot of pain in the more advanced maps! Remember to use it with unlocked targetting for the best results.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/f9f601c43ae993d23011377239cbd389886ae0e5.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Early Diaries #13 Leaderboards
notes.content:
So, we promised them, we're delivering them. Empires in Ruins finally has its leaderboard. I know that it might feel a thing of vanity, but let me tell you why I wanted to implement them.
The idea came for the first time, eons ago, when I was playing Anomaly, by 11bit Studios (great game btw).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/6bb59ddfbe10d3e454a51593dbf5837c5e258f36.jpg[/img]

Each map had its own leaderboard, and upon defeating it, you could see your ranking. I am not much into score attack or competitive games, but damn, I did replay more than a few maps, just to get into a better position. It felt kinda unexpected and silly to me, but I loved it.
And so I thought, why not having them for Empires in Ruins as well? They are now available in multiple formats. In the menu screens, you get a summary leaderboards of your position among friends that own and play the game. It rotates among Campaign, Sandbox and Arcade mode (the sum of all best map results for the latter).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/71ce5e4eae001339279098b7ddcd935e7bb3f199.jpg[/img]

That said, time to brutally humiliate your friends on those boards, don't you think?
For the Campaign and Sandbox, I had to insert a specific scoring system, here you have it, for clarity.

Campaign  Score Calculation
[i]Per battle won >> +Battle score
Per battle lost >> -1000
Per autoresolve won >> +500
Per autoresolve lost >> -500
Per event prevented >> +100
Per officer investigated with success >> +100
Per rebellion quelled in a province with success >> +100
Per chapter completed +1000
Per research unlocked +50
Per province with Rebellion below 5% at the end of the game >> +100
Per provicne with Authority or Happiness above 75% at the end of the game >> +100
Per province with Rebellion above 50% at the end of the game >> -100
Per provicne with Authority or Happiness below 30% at the end of the game >> -100
Per tribute successfully paid >> +500
Per tribute failed >> -500
Per settlment upgraded >> 100
Tributes active >> +15% total
Riots active (Sandbox only) >> +15% total
Easy >> 85%
Intermediate >> 100%
Hardcore >> 120%[/i]

Now off you trot, I have a Tech Tree for Arcade mode to implement, one new beautiful view of the Settlements for the campaign, and one month and half left of our Early Access! See you soon!
Cheers,
Dr.H

notes.title: Early Dev Diaries #12 Research Queue
notes.content:
I remember well one complain that while "minor" was mentioned a lot of times, specially in the first few months of review. At first it did sound a bit weird to be honest, then I understood.
The aforementioned complain was "it's weird to have a loading screen to open the research screen". I gotta admit, I didn't understand why it was that weird.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/80a5d30a35d9cf4725bec6a556f687145a6c476a.jpg[/img]

At that time, it was possible to set for research one technology at time though, that meant that specially if you had a good research points output and you were researching cheap techs, you might have had to go back and forth to the the Research screen quite a few times. Once every 2-3 turns maybe. Oh well, then I can understand why the loading panel might get in the way.
The research screen is on a separate scene for performance reasons, too long to explain, but let's say that this way, the game is a lot more robust and optimized in terms of RAM above all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/66962880d3e15cdd283f5ea0955b8953a03f27c8.jpg[/img]

But how to solve that problem? Well, the answer is simple. Don't have the player have to go back to research that often, so what better than a queue in which to enqueue several researches to so minimize the trips to the engineer? 
It took as while because we had a lot higher priority tasks set, but now you finally get your well deserved research queue!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/ba3c43848c7be47992920a1e8b65424078b61c34.jpg[/img]

It has 5 slots (plus the slot of the currently researched tech, so 6 in total), it warns you in the main campaign screen when it's empty, it does display a preview in the same screen (just hover the Tech icon on the lower bar) and allows you to add and remove elements at your pleasure. What more could you ask for from a Research Queue?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/3b775aceb93b9f4458adfb6637b37a70e8e3f029.jpg[/img]

That said, now back to work, next we get started with th-

Anyway, also quite a few fixes.

notes.title: DevLog Helps us deciding what feature to develop next!
notes.content:
Hello guys, how's everyone doing! We had a hell of a week because we did release our latest published and produced game (developed by Vikerlane), Headbangers in Holiday Hell, and now we're back full power onto Empires in Ruins. We're still fixing a handful of the latest bugs or recommended polishes received from you guys, and it's now time to take a decision on the next month of development. 

We have two main big features to take on, and we'd really like to hear what you think about it, so that you can also contribute to what's coming next on the game (Full release is being planned for the second half of march, so it's not that far away at all anymore!)

The decision is between a big feature(s) for the Arcade branch, or for the Campaign/Sandbox branch. Mind, both will be done anyway, we are just deciding in which order!

[b]Arcade branch[/b]
[list]
[*] Tech tree tailored to Arcade mode (using victory stars to unlock upgrades)
[*] Leaderboards (global and per map)
[/list]

[b]Campaign/Sandbox branch[/b]
[list]
[*] Settlement HOMM-like visual development
[*] Additional information from pre-battle scouting
[/list]

That would mean, shall we add Tech Tree and leaderboards to the Arcade mode first, or shall we instead add the visual development of the settlement (HOMM-style) and the additional scouting to Campaign and Sandbox?
Production-wise, it doesn't make much of a difference for us, so that's why we'd love to go with you guys might like best first!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/09eb43a492c6b32a4fd26467736e6eb30c812865.png[/img]

[b]Tribute System design notes[/b]

Description: In order to see the progress in taming the rebelling provinces, the Crown demands to see the tithes restored from the Western Marches. Therefore the Commander will have to send, periodically and in growing size, a tribute in gold and resouces to the capital. Succeeding at it will reinforce its authority and the morale of men, failing at it will have the opposite effect, up to leading to the removal of the Commander from the campaign lead and his hanging. After being introduced by a dialog with Sgt.Vunstenberg, a new recurring timer will be following the player for the whole duration of the campaign (In sandbox mode the timer begins on turn 10).

Timer: Every 30 turns (i.e. 15 days) the Player HAS to pay a tribute in Gold, Wood, Stone and Iron of growing entity with each iteration. 
Enity: To be decided yet.

Gameplay conditions: 
* IF a Tribute is paid timely, for the next 30 turns the player will benefit of a +5% to Authority in all the Controlled provinces, and a +5% Morale to towers in battle (Morale increases the chance of a tower of causing double damage with a hit).
* IF a Tribute is not paid timely, for the next 30 turns the player will receive a -5% to Authority in all the controller provinces and a -5% Morale to towers in battle (Very low morale provides towers with a chance to cause halved damage in battle with a hit)
* IF the player fails to pay 3(5?) Times a tribute, the campaign is over and the Commander is removed from his position.
* Relations with the crown do influence the entity of the tribute ( above 50 each point provides a -0.5%, below 50% each point provides a +0.5%)

UI Elements: 
* On-screen UI timer to next tribute with clickable button.
* Detailed tributes window (Accessible through the on-screen button) with details about: Current modifiers, Paid and Failed tributes, Entity of the Next Tribute and missing/exceeding resources.
* Interactive UI to Pay or to Refuse to Pay (or to confirm the lack of resources and the failure in paying the tribute).




[b]Instant Buying System for provinces [/b]

Description: Allow the player to use globally gathered resources to instantly buy a province asset already in production queue. 

Gameplay conditions: ONE asset per turn can be instantly built in a province upon paying a fairly high cost in resouces (approximately 10 times the normal value of the asset).

UI Elements:
* Button added to the building queue near the Currently Built asset
* UI Panel with details on next/current payment, prediction of achieved resources with current economy, payment option and displayed failed payments.



[b]Market System[/b]

notes.title: Early Dev Diaries #10 - Tributes, Assets and Markets
notes.content:
We got asked a few times to add depth to the economic system of the game campaign and sandbox mode. We did gather a few months of feedback now, and here's what we boiled out of that.  The instant-buying system was already planned for the province assets (btw, sneak a peek at the upcoming provinces management screens too!), but the Tribute and the Market, were designed during the last couple of months and they are now in pre-beta phase. 1-2 weeks and they will enter public beta and then go into the main branch soon after that!

If you guys are interested into being part of the design process, don't hesitate to contact us on [url=https://discord.gg/eir]Discord [/url] or write us on the discussions forum and we'll be super happy to hear your feedback/contributions/ideas (be realistic though, we can't apply everything we hear :heimer: )

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/446b88e88869702e32903be5afb31faf5ef566ec.png[/img]

Here's some of my design notes about what's coming! PS there will still be some changes in some details and specs, based on testing and feedback of course!

[h1]Tribute System design notes[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/8196120acaf282c0c7a2943d3a51788bb96ae385.png[/img]

[b]Description: [/b]In order to see the progress in taming the rebelling provinces, the Crown demands to see the tithes restored from the Western Marches. Therefore the Commander will have to send, periodically and in growing size, a tribute in gold and resouces to the capital. Succeeding at it will reinforce its authority and the morale of men, failing at it will have the opposite effect, up to leading to the removal of the Commander from the campaign lead and his hanging. After being introduced by a dialog with Sgt.Vunstenberg, a new recurring timer will be following the player for the whole duration of the campaign (In sandbox mode the timer begins on turn 10).

Timer: Every 30 turns (i.e. 15 days) the Player HAS to pay a tribute in Gold, Wood, Stone and Iron of growing entity with each iteration. 
Enity: To be decided yet.
[b]
Gameplay conditions: [/b]
* IF a Tribute is paid timely, for the next 30 turns the player will benefit of a +5% to Authority in all the Controlled provinces, and a +5% Morale to towers in battle (Morale increases the chance of a tower of causing double damage with a hit).
* IF a Tribute is not paid timely, for the next 30 turns the player will receive a -5% to Authority in all the controller provinces and a -5% Morale to towers in battle (Very low morale provides towers with a chance to cause halved damage in battle with a hit)
* IF the player fails to pay 3(5?) Times a tribute, the campaign is over and the Commander is removed from his position.
* Relations with the crown do influence the entity of the tribute ( above 50 each point provides a -0.5%, below 50% each point provides a +0.5%)
[b]
UI Elements: [/b]
* On-screen UI timer to next tribute with clickable button.
* Detailed tributes window (Accessible through the on-screen button) with details about: Current modifiers, Paid and Failed tributes, Entity of the Next Tribute and missing/exceeding resources.
* Interactive UI to Pay or to Refuse to Pay (or to confirm the lack of resources and the failure in paying the tribute).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/80ef8064ad5146bd0a1baa5cbda8f1094d7c2c7d.png[/img]

[h1]Instant Buying System for provinces [/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/cd7bef9afdfd397a057b0cbdfba8191f9e0c9d59.png[/img]

[b]Description: [/b]Allow the player to use globally gathered resources to instantly buy a province asset already in production queue. 

[b]Gameplay conditions[/b]: ONE asset per turn can be instantly built in a province upon paying a fairly high cost in resouces (approximately 10 times the normal value of the asset).

[b]UI Elements:[/b]
* Button added to the building queue near the Currently Built asset
* UI Panel with details on next/current payment, prediction of achieved resources with current economy, payment option and displayed failed payments.

[h1]Market System[/h1]

[b]Description : [/b]Once the player builds at least one Market in one of the provinces, he has access to the Marketplace to exchange resources for gold and viceversa.

[b]Gameplay conditions: [/b]Only activates when the player has built at least one Market asset. The default exchange ratio is 2:1 (resources to gold) and 2:1 (gold to resources). With each market tier built, this exchange rate improves (in favor of the player) by 2% to a maximum of 2:1.9.

[b]UI elements :[/b]
* UI button to reach the market from the main campaign screen, and from the Tribute system.
* UI panel with sliders and methods to exchange resources (gold vs resources and viceversa)

notes.title: Early Access Diaries #7 Past, present and future
notes.content:
Game Settings are in, tested and uploaded, Steam Achievements are almost ready, Files for Localization are being prepared, it looks like we're sticking to the roadmap and it's time to summarize a bit how it did go these first 3 months of Early Access.
First of all, we're still delighted that our Reviews rating is stable at 100% positives. We know, it will change at some point, it's unavoidable, but we got quite some shivers by reading very positive reviews of our work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/e726f33a4b6b0346390ea734f8b06172bc3c2b56.png[/img]

We've been working a lot on our feedback (and your bug reports too), and what we did focus the most is how to make sure all the parts of the game are fully enjoyable.
We think we found some minor weaknesses on the main campaign loop, and even though we already addressed them in several ways, that's what we wanna do next.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/6a74dce14a1d37074267ebab78944c705db16348.png[/img]

[b]Recurring Riots.[/b]
Some of you told us that for the way they play, they would love to have a way to completely avoid an upcoming riot.
Even if to achieve that it might take more work than fighting the riot itself.
To address this, we are designing a system to negotiate and/or bribe a way out of a recurring riot. It won't be neither easy nor cheap, but it will provide you one more option on the table to better fit your gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/0f94f60ddf79b7d080a425c4d638f45a4392f964.jpg[/img]

[b]Recurring Tributes.[/b]
In order to help balancing out resources in a flavorful way, we will be adding recurring Tributes to the Crown Prince. These will be large sums of gold and resources that need to be reached by a given turn. If you do reach them, they will be subtracted from your total, but you will receive a solid bonus in terms of morale of your troops, relations with the Crown and efficiency of your province assets. Failing to achieve the request, will leave you without resources left, with a very low morale and a drop in efficiency of your provinces (but hey, the Rebels will appreciate you more for that).
Failing to fullfill a certain number of tribute (we are still brainstorming on the amount, but 5 might be the target), will cause you to lose the game, while fullfilling them all continuously might provide cumulative bonuses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/85b640530740fdefa87abd9d75829d687e0f13b5.jpg[/img]

The two above were not planned as features, and have been originated from your input and feedback. The other big ones coming, that were already in the roadmap, but that people di ask fairly often, are worth being remembered and are the following ones:
[list]
[*] We are adding an instant-buy system with resources for province assets. It will be quite expensive, quite a few times it will be priceless to have it accessible!
[*] We are adding a research queue. We know you want it, we know it's needed, we are gonna get it there so that you don't have to go back and forth from the research screen.
[*] We're working on a HOMM-like province view and building screen with ALL the province assets, each with its three levels of upgrades. A delight for the eyes (check the preview pic)
[*] Sandbox is getting a slow but large redesign, that will be adding some more sense of progression and some more tasks and objectives. We can't spoil more yet, and it will still take some time, but you will love it!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/f95173cc0176a28c45bb3319bd4511f1ae1e25d2.jpg[/img]

That said, a little summary of what we did since the last post

notes.title: Early Access Diaries #6 Deeper, faster, harder
notes.content:
Yes, we didn't push many updates during the last week, but it's mostly because we're deep into game settings.

notes.title: Impending Riots and ways to delay those Riots
notes.content:
The Western Marches are aflame with rebellion and riots. Don't let a single, temporarily tamed, province deceive you at times. They are not happy, they are not
welcoming you. In the best cases, they are trying their best to tolerate you.
That said, for most of the game, riots will keep on happening periodically. We are working on a system to distribute them even better based on provinces stats, and even to determine
their duration and strenght based on each province rebellion, but you can't stop them (well, you can, but that's a story we won't spoil).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/fcd75ac05be13fc63161b47fdc2365ab6a94536f.jpg[/img]

You can't stop them, but you can delay them, though. Let's see how riots work first.

Once the riot timer has started (since a specific dialog in the Campaign, or since the first turn in Sandbox mode), the system determines a 
pseudorandom number of turns to next riot, based on the difficulty.  14 to 18 in Easy mode, 9 to 12 in Intermediate mode, and 4 to 6 in Hard mode.

This base timer, is modified as follow by the % of achieved chapter objectives (this only works in Campaign mode):
[list]
[*] 25% Objectives  +1
[*] 50% Objectives  +2
[*] 75% Objectives  +3
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/188e6b9069a398bdc09d19830ef6a6387b4d47ae.jpg[/img]

Your relations with the Folks also impact this timer: 
[list]
[*] -1 for each 10 points below 50%
[*] +1 for each 10 points above 50%
[/list]

Conquering or losing a province, gives a one time bonus or malus to the timer instead, also based on the game difficulty.

[b]Conquering province : [/b]
[list]
[*] +9 (Easy)
[*] +5(Intermediate)
[*] +3 (hard)
[/list]
[b]Losing province: [/b]
[list]
[*] -2 (Easy)
[*] -4 (Intermediate)
[*] -6 (hard)
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/081b8cf0721983d745037fa344b1d36654eb68d0.jpg[/img]

In order to avoid an excessive unbalancing of the game though, the maximum number of turns to the next riot is limited to the following values. 
(Conquering a province will add bonus turns, but it will still have this value as a maximum cap).

Max Turns to Next riot
[list]
[*] Easy: 20
[*] Intermediate: 15
[*] Hard: 8
[/list]

Summarizing, if you[b] stay friendly with the Folks[/b] and [b]work towards achieving your chapter objectives[/b], and [b]distribute wisely your conquest of the 
Marches[/b], riots will be a lot less frequent than if you don't do all the above. Easy no?

If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask!
Cheers,
Dr.H

notes.title: Early Access Diaries #3 - Juggernauting around
notes.content:
We're a bit late this time, but I told you last time that I was gonna be semi-off the grid for a few days. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/d4c2c31afb01d621dc361b2dba5f14d9b8d99817.jpg[/img]

I've been working on EiR code from a tiny village on the italian Alps, it was very relaxing, and surprisingly the upload speed of my 4G there allowed me to upload the game builds fairly quickly too.

But ok, all that is probably not that interesting for you, let's move to cooler stuff now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/2b8883e40ddfb8c7f729421825e2806b668bfbf8.jpg[/img]

First of all, we're stocked with the quality of our gamers. You guys are awesome. You're being patient, playing incredibly well, and using the feedback tool to report bugs and problems a lot (that and the forum).
And, we're being as fast as possible in fixing things too! Not even one month that the game is out, and already we made 10 updates, fixing endless problems, from major to minor. This is exactly how we expected the first month of Early Access to be. Things are now slowing down luckily, you guys keep on playing, but bugs reports are less and less frequent (hopefully because there's less bugs ?lunar2019grinningpig? )

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/07f0640fe0a51f4fdff691cec8a1204acdc9f46b.png[/img]

We had more than 400 hours of pre-release testing, but like it always happens in IT, and specially in a non-linear game, the moment you guys took on the Western Marches, you managed to find the craziest and most hidden bugs ever! And we fixed them!

[*] Fixed a bug with Destroyed assets and building queues

[*] Lowered Chapter 3 and 4 requirements of Authority to 50 (from 60%) and Happiness to 40 (from 50%)

notes.title: Governors - Of men and beasts
notes.content:
Empires in Ruins is set in a very very corrupted world. And even more, it's set in one of the most corrupted kingdoms in this world. If that was not enough, we picked one of the most degenerated and corrupted areas of that kingdom to set the campaign.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/f24520a6a11553fe7332a520a9193248f010f381.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/d8231be3b00530d815754e2a9498585d269371cc.jpg[/img]

That said, your Officers couldn't be a well groomed handful of choir boys. They are an unreliable bunch at best, that you need to keep tamed with bribery, investigations and trips to the gallow. Here's some more details about how their mechanics work in game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/09f90f155cac94af1eb3e6f9d734a1718a6872f0.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] Each governor has a Loyalty value that goes from 0 to 5 stars (and translates into a % value)
[*] Each governor has a Rank (that currently is not gonna change, but during the Officers update will allow them to grow in experience during the campaign). Based on the rank they do have better or worse skills, loyalty and more or less feats.
[*] The first time you meet a governor, a check is made automatically, based on your Empathy and Leadership, to determine if the loyalty is know or not
[*] If loyalty is not known yet, [b]you can investigate an officer[/b]. Investigations use your [b]Empathy and Leadership values[/b] to determine the success chance. In case of a province governor, also the province espionage is used.
[*] If investigations fail, they will further lower the governor loyalty and you will still not know the value
[*] You can[b] bribe a governor[/b] to temporarily increase his loyalty
[*] The relations with the officer faction do influence the officer loyalty
[*] If you succeed in hanging (he might still escape) an officer, his faction relations will lower, but the loyalty of all the other officers will improve for a while (fear helps a lot)
[*] As of now, loyalty mostly matters for Governor and not for Battle Board officers
[*] A disloyal officer will [b]secretly steal money from the province[/b] he governs, and will secretly increase the rebellion in the province
[*] An officer will[b] obey his orders about the building queue based on his loyalty[/b]. A disloyal officer will often build nothing or build the wrong things
[*] A disloyal officer can [b]betray you[/b], cause a riot in the province and run with the money
[*] When you conquer a province, there's a chance that the province governor decided to join (based on your Empathy and Leadership). These governors will always belong to the Folks (Rebels) faction.
[*] Your Officers Board only provides bonuses in battle. It will influence the basic stats for towers (Damage, Range, Firerate and Morale), and based on the Officers feats, it will also add a variety of modifiers.
[/list]

Additionally here's how Leadership does influence the maximum rank and maximum number of officers that you can hire.

Maximum rank available:
[list]
[*] Hire officers of Rank 0 >> Leadership>0%
[*] Hire officers of Rank 1 >> Leadership>30%
[*] Hire officers of Rank 2 >> Leadership>50%
[/list]

Maximum number of hired officers:
[list]
[*] 0-15 >> 3 Officers
[*] 16-25 >> 7 Officers
[*] 26-45 >> 12 Officers
[*] 46-60 >> 20 Officers
[*] 61-75 >> 25 Officers
[*] 76-100 >> 30 Officers
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/05d27d52927861b79ddcfd4a27b85272eb311d43.jpg[/img]

Hopefully this will give you a few more insights about your officers and how to use them!
Cheers,
Dr.H, Lead Dev

notes.title: Roadmap to Early Access
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/611182d0d062fb32850bc3c304bf92e4a32cea9b.png[/img]

During the years, most people did grow (rightfully) skeptical about Early Access games. The failure stories and the big disappointments of the past left a bit mark on this type of release.

We like to think that Empires in Ruins EA is different. Well, first of all, we are releasing an already playable game, with very few bugs left (and mostly minor) and with almost the full contents of the final one. All the battle maps, the full campaign, all the enemies, buildings and towers, and for a lesser price than the final product.

So you might ask why Early Access if the product it's almost final, why didn't we wait further and release it normally? Well, consider this: Empires in Ruins is in the making since 5-6 years now, and we reached a point in which not even our wide set of testers is wide any longer for us to give the game the final polishing balancing and modding it needs to shine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/a9a93a23a3273c7efb9ca737025b7ab7801cff8b.jpg[/img]

There is also an additional set of optional and aesthetic features that we want to get in, but we didn't have time for yet, so focused we were on finishing the core game.
With our pre-release out to youtubers and streamers (let me spoit it for you, most people are loving it ːheimerː ), we noticed a few things that are missing, a few that could be better, and some ways we could enhance the fun (specially in the Sanbox mode).

But that's a lot of words, let me give you a few details on how it will work

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/314eb597ebfbaed637f85d652bd9088a55ada8c7.png[/img]

* Weekly, a dev blog entry, here and on our website, about the week progress
* Every two weeks, a developer stream with some tricks, insights and progress achieved
* A freely accessible beta branch for whoever wants to try, test and contribute
* An ingame feedback system (already available) for feedback and bugs reports
* The game has embedded analytics (you can opt out if you don't want them) that allow us to track some stats in order to better balance the game (victories vs defeats, duration of battles, etc).
* In the roadmap, we marked the larger updates batches, but each sub-update will go online as soon as tested. We prefered not to detail each one specifically because A) would have been edlessly long to read B) we need the flexibility to adapt to technical challenges that might arise (welcome to programmer's life).

The first update (final deadline in May) will included

* [b]Steam Achievements[/b]
>> 50+ Steam Achievements in all gameplay modes
* [b]Game Settings[/b]
>> Video, Audio, Controls (includes keys remapping), Gameplay Settings
* [b]Sandbox Update #1[/b]
>> Introducing enemy hostile attacks, timed tasks and progression unlocks in Sandbox mode
* [b]Asian Language Localization[/b]
>> Traditional Chinese, Modern Chinese, Japanese, Korean

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/7b0580468af26527a33390d054d4bd5011c6a20d.png[/img]

That said, this is taken from our website as I write, so, well, no pressure ːlunar2019grinningpigː!
Going back to work now, if you guys have questions or feedback already, please don't hesitate to write on our forum, join our discord, or contact us directly!

Cheers,
Dr.H, Lead Designer

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/13a8a81747c7bf76bc90999faefea7c556e94252.png[/img]

So, the demo is out! And guess what, it had a classic day 1 bug. Unbelievable, one week testing it, then at the last minute a small fix in order to prevent the loading of the wrong save files, and.... BADUM TSSSS: all of a sudden it's impossible to start a new Campaign.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/1a771e14f681c1907a1109b0cda2f2d1d191d9cc.png[/img]

And this is where we really need to thank our ingame feedback system: some good soul luckily reported it, and fixing it was trivial, a matter of a couple of minutes. So now the first Day 1 patch it's officially up, and the game officially works (luckily Arcade mode had worked since the beginning).

Still, we should wear sackcloth and ashes for such a dumb mistake, but well, at least it's fixed ːsteamhappyː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/1a595c981ff8e5b8820e6e3674deda00d0b39207.png[/img]

What's in the demo you will ask. Will you ask? Well, in case you will, here's the demo content:

* The first part of the campaign, including intro, dialogs, 5 battle maps and up to 25 turns of management.
* 5 Arcade maps to play as many times as you wish in all difficulties
* The "famed" Map 26, our workbench map, not part of the game but used to develop and test it, with [b]ALL THE TOWERS[/b] and [b]ALL THE ENEMIES[/b] so to see how the game evolves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/56bd8bd8fce4ea66757035e512e59d257b19207e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/199c82c4b2959171e43e8a5722d2115b15fd41a3.png[/img]

That said, we hope you like it, and we really look forward to hear what you think about it! 
Talk to you soon!
Dr.H, Lead Dev

notes.title: End of november - Updates
notes.content:
It's closing in, we can almost hear the clock ticking. Can you imagine how we do feel? After more than [b]5 years[/b] working on [u][b]Empires in Ruins[/b][/u], the moment of truth is approaching, release is near!

[h1][i][b]4th February 2020[/b][/i][/h1]

Mark this date, this time is real. After endless delays and uncountable hours of work from our team, Empires in Ruins is getting revved up for release. Yes, it's an Early Access release, but the game is very very close to its final state.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/e66200cc6e6314f8cbbb6de7246d266842a8abd1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/199c82c4b2959171e43e8a5722d2115b15fd41a3.png[/img]

The latest build does include:

[list]
[*] The [b]full game campaign[/b] (5 chapters, 26 battlefields, more than 30 dialogs, 10+ hours of gameplay)
[*] [b]All the 26 maps[/b] available [b]in arcade mode[/b]
[*] [b]Sandbox mode[/b] with free roaming map
[*] [b]All the 100+ technologies[/b] unlocks
[*] [b]All the 23 buildings and the 20 enemies[/b]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/eec6717e0b46a1d00c17206c5bbedb63c657cac7.png[/img]

What's missing (and it will be added during the Early access period) is:
[list]
[*] Manually controlled research tree for arcade mode (Current unlocks are fixed and based on each map difficulty)
[*] The province assets visualization (HOMM-like)
[*] Additional scouting modes and information
[*] A queue system for the research tree (in Campaign and Sandbox mode)
[*] Localization (Confirmed languages this far: Italian, Greek, German, French, Chinese Traditional, Chinese Modern, Korean, Japanese)
[*] Further balancing, polishing and minor aesthetic fixes and features
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/29d0de7b4c762a0e14446bb70421b0d8aad2d6ce.png[/img]

That said, in approximately one week, we will release a [b]free demo[/b] on Steam, because first of all we want to excited you and tease you (the saves will be mostly compatible with the full game), but we also want people to know what EiR is about. Being a quite unique mix of genres, we think it's much better for people to try, so those that love it can stay, those that don't like it don't have to waste further time on it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32563868/a43cd1d5c1c6f9cf7aa1a61d29c6fbcf99d0de29.png[/img]

Now guys, we're off to development, see you very soon around! 

PS, have you considered joining our [url=http://discord.gg/eir]Official Discord Server[/url] to be part of the development (also, Emiliano gives away his secret recipes for homebrewing and cooking on a channel there ;) ) ?

notes.title: Sergeant Hans Heimer - Character progression
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/e0639420ebd9520b379128826ba10ee84c8383cf.png[/img]

While far from being an RPG game, Empires in Ruins puts quite some focus on Sergeant Hans Heimer, the main character. During the campaign, battles, characters and events tend to be seen with the grumpy eyes of the Sergeant, often foggy from brandy and temper.

The presence of Heimer on a battlefield or on a given province during a certain turn, will unlock abilities and modifiers otherwise not usable. During the campaign, Heimer will grow in experience and level in a fairly classic RPG progress style.


Almost each successful action taken provides a varying amount of experience points. From winning a battle to preventing a rebellious event, etc.


The maximum reachable level is 20, and each 3 levels, starting from the 3rd one, the player will unlock one of the cooldown abilities that can be used in battle.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/3e6077b3ad3e12c3e0086ea031fd6454217b8a2b.png[/img]


Unlock Cooldown skills (usable in battle) at:
[list]
[*][u]Lvl 3[/u] [u]Double shifts[/u][/*]
[*][u]Lvl 6[/u] [u]Shouting&Bullying (Can only be used when Heimer's leading the battle)[/u][/*]
[*]Lvl 9 [u]Pocket Money[/u][/*]
[*]Lvl 12 [u]Loot the corpses[/u][/*]
[*]Lvl 15 [u]Throw them Everything we have[/u][/*]
[*]Lvl 18 [u]Call the Charge[/u][/*]
[/list]

With each level obtained, the character receives 7 to 5 (according to the difficulty level) stat points to distribute among its 4 main stats (Leadership, Empathy, Tactics, Management). No stat can be taken past 100%.

[h1][u]Leadership[/u][/h1]
The grip that Heimer has on his soldier and on the population. It influences:
[list]
[*]Number of Knights (Call the Charge).[/*]
[*]Level and number of officers.[/*]
[*]Efficiency of bribing officers.[/*]
[*]Officers loyalty.[/*]
[*]Convert a conquered governor.[/*]
[*]Prevent rebellious events.[/*]
[*]Headquarter Authority bonus.[/*]
[*]Shouting and Bullying efficiency.[/*]
[/list]

[h1][u]Tactics[/u][/h1]
Sarge tactical ability on the battlefield. It impacts:
[list]
[*]Knights Damage (Call the Charge)[/*]
[*]Firerate bonus (Throw 'em Everything we Have)[/*]
[*]Tower and soldiers damage[/*]
[*]Headquarter Authority bonus[/*]
[/list]

[h1][u]Empathy[/u][/h1]
Heimer's renown social skills in dealing with people.It affects: 
[list]
[*]Success chance in Officer investigations[/*]
[*]Converting a governor from a conquered province[/*]
[*]Determine Officer loyalty on first meeting[/*]
[*]Headquarter Happiness bonus[/*]
[*]Officers loyalty[/*]
[*]Prevent rebellious events[/*]
[/list]

[h1][u]Management[/u][/h1]
While management and logistic are not Heimer's cup of brandy, he either learns something about it or face quite some issues.It influences:
[list]
[*]Effect duration (Double shifts)[/*]
[*]Efficiency (Double shifts)[/*]
[*]Gold cost (Pocked Money)[/*]
[*]Headquarter resources production bonus[/*]
[*]Headquarter Food production bonus[/*]
[/list]

[u]A fifth stat can't be influenced by the player and is only influenced by events and other specific in game situations[/u]

[h1][u]Luck[/u][/h1]
You can't influence Luck, but luck has no problem in influencing you. Every time there is a chance for random occurrence, Luck will be influencing it. Make sure you step on the right amount of horse crap, it's said to bring good luck.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/6bd30322bab790bb12d4151446bf91b2f0d2efc9.png[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/543f25d272b9f37a69ea157f66bf1c317e47a4a0.png[/img]

Beside the stats described above, Heimer's characterized by his relations with the factions at play in the campaign. First of all the internal faction of the Principality of Koth: Crown (representing the will of Prince Von Karlstein I), the Kothian Army (led by General Von Blutbergen) and the Church of Kaer (in the person of Archbishop Von Siemens-Gotsler).


[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/2bcb5fcd148fc7c7b667690c17dfe23120d22fef.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/58b106de19939b3922912e1a21deb1d39088fe8c.png[/img][/url][url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/733e1e12b70f5c3bf630f655333770c65e7a0acb.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/39ff06a0ab04bc8944e6e6e1a3cc5e8059443087.png[/img][/url][url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/6f3b5e7dc85adf0360eb62e0deb993c0fc7d0ed6.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/c7514ba35d90eed7b1d3f158a9ee8ef901063245.png[/img][/url]

Then the relations with the folks of the Western Marches, and with the enemy forces as well, the Krovan Kingdom. The values do influence the loyalty of officers belonging to one or another.


So, from EiR land that was it, see you next time
Dr.H,Lead Designer

notes.title: Progress Update, UIs work progressing.
notes.content:
Few things (well, more than few, but these are among the star ones) can make or break a game as easily as the quality of its UIs. Whereas a smart, clean and good looking UI, easy to use and intuitive (and with the proper amount of tooltips and info) can make any boarding and following gaming experience pleasant, the opposite is even more true for badly made UIs.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/aad8022d85db203776b60c5c9a8cb452c0084586.jpg[/img]


Overwhelm the gamer with heavy-to-read UIs with ugly visuals and clogged layouts, and the chance that he will be quitting pretty soon the game is very high. And it’s almost sure it will happen if the game is a strategy game.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/67aaa6479f85f1058a48ea866ee1fd11e4e8f249.png[/img]


While other genres can get away with not-so-good UIs, strategy games definitely can’t. Our very early UIs in Empires were of the ugly kind, even worst if that is possible.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/b14c361396a707da59f95a7b22b54e6789a1c8c0.jpg[/img]

At development time, unless you have a UX/UI designer integrated in the team since the beginning, it’s very hard to produce good UIs on the first attempt. The temptation is usually to provide as much information as possible to the player, never realizing that this ends up flooding the information layers and rendering them all uselessly anonymous. Less is more, that is a hard rule to nail for programmers mostly.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/3f6dc1d8c4ea49bea1a826088a198850911e0d45.jpg[/img]

So now, with the help of a friend that did sketch for us the new layouts, we’re onto remaking the UIs. A few rules of thumb we are adopting in doing that:

[list]
[*]Less is more
[*]Readable fonts, sharp contrasts
[*]Well distinguisheable icons/buttons
[*]Use shapes and styles to let the player familiarize with elements
[*]Wider breath in the layouts and elements distribution
[*]Use a coherent style even while having several different elements styles
[/list]

In the gallery above you can see some WIPs of the new UIs, we will not show the old ones out of shame though.

One last thing worth mentioning though, it’s the approach we are taking to the battle maps UIs.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32563868/f5804bd27c75af4524431841976e8265fe1f5cc5.png[/img]

Following the whole EiR approach to visuals (pre-rendered 3D to 2D sprites), we are going the same why for the UIs of the battle map. That is, our of the sketches we are modeling 3D UIs, once modeled and ready, we render them out back to 2D textures and use them as such. The last picture above shows a very early example of that, and it shouldn’t take too long before we manage to show you the real deal.

Until then, have a blast guys,

Ahhh wait! We also just did finish the new Website and Mailing list! Check it out

[url=www.empiresinruins.com] www.empiresinruins.com [/url]

Cheers,
Emiliano, @DokHgn, Lead Dev
